```python
>>> import ipaddress
>>> ipaddress.ip_network('192.0.2.100')
IPv4Network('192.0.2.100/32')
```
Offhand, I'm not sure if we could implement a workaround django-cockroachdb or if CockroachDB may consider adding https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/18846 to the list of tasks for psycopg3 support. \cc @rafiss

https://github.com/apollo13/django/pull/4 should address your concerns @dvarrazzo.

I have reservations about the arguments provided in the thread in a context where Django has always configured its psycopg connections in a way to make them work with its public ORM API first and that usage of custom types and raw queries will have to be adapted anyway by advanced users to migrate to psycopg 3.

Both approaches provide escape hatches, defaulting to treating `str` literals as `::text` only happens to be more friendly to `Expression` subclassers which the public API Django supports. Even if _Django ORM had this nice characteristic_ it was never something that was part of the public API and thus we cannot assess the impact of the changes beyond our own anecdotal evidence.  

Users of raw queries will have to adapt their queries anyway when using string literals that previously worked seamlessly e.g.

```
INSERT INTO table(json_field) VALUES(%s)
```

Won't work anymore for encoded JSON as string literals as the `Jsonb` adaptations changes in this PR demonstrated. That's the reason why it felt natural to me to follow the same approach when dealing with `citext` and `spheroid`.

body:
We could make `IntegerField.get_db_prep_value` call into a new `connection.ops.adapt_integerfield_value(value, self.get_internal_type())` method that embeds this logic.

I suspect this would also solve somewhat of [an undesirable effect/borderline DoS vector the lack of explicit typing for integer values on PostgreSQL causes](https://code.jeremyevans.net/2022-11-01-forcing-sequential-scans-on-postgresql.html) that can be exploited in most Django setups out there e.g. think of `\d+` or `<int:pk>` [that accepts unbounded values](https://github.com/django/django/blob/3d3e955efaaeb4cc968e522592c5c1e47bdc72c4/django/urls/converters.py#L6) and are usually looked up against indexed columns which currently results in FTS.

It comes at the cost of an extra function call for every integer literal though which could have some noticeable effects on queries that use a lot of such values (e.g. think of prefetching or other source of `filter(integer_field__in=[...])`).

All that to say that even if it incurs a cost there's likely a security rationale to do so. It could be done in many different ways (e.g. by having `Value.as_sql` raise an `EmptyResultSet` when a value is outside of the allowed range) but since this is a Postgres specific issue and `EmptyResultSet` comes with its own can of worms it might be better to simply to pay the performance degradation tax in the name of security enforcement and reap the benefits here in terms of proper abstractions?

Looked into it, if anyone's interested (TL;DR - it's fine).

I believe the TimestamptzLoader is meant to replace this code in psycopg2 backend `create_cursor`:

```py
def create_cursor(self, name=None):
    ... snipped ...
    cursor.tzinfo_factory = self.tzinfo_factory if settings.USE_TZ else None
    return cursor

def tzinfo_factory(self, offset):                                           
    return self.timezone
```

In psycopg2 the `tzinfo_factory` line has this effect when loading a timestamptz (see [code](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg2/blob/0b01ded426b7423621af68d9fc33e532a5bda4a7/psycopg/typecast_datetime.c#L136)):

1. If `USE_TZ = False`, returns a naive datetime in DB connection timezone - equivalent to reading aware datetime from DB and doing `replace(tzinfo=None)`.
2. If `USE_TZ = True`, returns an aware datetime in DB connection timezone and replaces its timezone to Django DB timezone - equivalent to doing `replace(tzinfo=self.timezone)`.

i.e. same as `TimestamptzLoader`'s `res.replace(tzinfo=self.timezone)` code. 

So this indeed relies on the assumption that Django DB timezone == connection timezone, which Django ensures when setting up a new connection.

I think that once psycopg2 support is dropped, this assumption could be dropped, making things less dangerous. But until then, it's better to keep the psycopg2 and 3 behaviors the same.
